other_conditions: Candidates must hold a Bachelor's degree in the relevant field (10+2+4) for M.F.Sc. admission

Minimum academic performance: at least 60 % marks or OGPA 6.5 out of 10 (or 3.25 out of 5 / 2.60 out of 4); for SC/ST candidates the threshold is 55 % or OGPA 6.0 out of 10 (or 3.0 out of 5 / 2.40 out of 4)

For Ph.D. programmes, candidates need B.F.Sc. & M.F.Sc. (4 + 2 years) or B.Sc. & M.Sc. (3 years) from CIFE (till 1995) with OGPA 7.5 out of 10 (3.75 out of 5) for General/OBC and OGPA 7.0 out of 10 (3.5 out of 5) for SC/ST

Alternatively, D.F.Sc. from CIFE is acceptable if the candidate holds a Bachelor’s degree in biological science and has two years of experience in fisheries development work after obtaining the D.F.Sc.
Sponsored candidates with an M.Sc. in Fish and Fisheries (or related disciplines) and at least two years of fisheries development experience are also eligible

Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) is only awarded to candidates who join the M.F.Sc. programme at an institute different from the one where they obtained their Bachelor's degree; change of subject for JRF is not permitted
Foreign students are exempted from appearing in the written test and interview; admission is based on bio‑data scrutiny and recommendation of the head of the concerned discipline
Continuation of the fellowship after the first year depends on maintaining the required OGPA each year
benefits_summary: JRF provides a monthly stipend of Rs 5760 (plus a Rs 6000 annual contingent grant) for M.F.Sc., while SRF offers Rs 7000 / Rs 5600 monthly (plus a Rs 10 000 annual contingent grant) for Ph.D. research.
